title: One-Pot Tomato & Lentil Macaroni
description: Macaroni and canned lentils simmer together in a simple tomato sauce for an inexpensive one-pot pantry dinner.
substitutions: Use small shells instead of elbow macaroni.
Use white beans instead of lentils.
Skip the cheese for a dairy-free pantry meal.

steps.text: Simmer the macaroni in the tomato broth.

cookSteps.text: Combine 8 ounces macaroni, 1 can diced tomatoes, 2 cups broth, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/2 teaspoon Italian seasoning in a large saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a lively simmer.
Cover loosely and cook 12–15 minutes, stirring several times, until the pasta is tender and most of the liquid is absorbed.
Stir in 1 drained can lentils and cook 3–5 minutes until hot. Stir in 1/2 cup cheese if using and serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat with a splash of broth or water.

title: Ham, Pea & Cheddar Egg Muffins
description: Eggs, diced ham, peas, and cheddar bake into easy individual breakfast cups that reheat well.
substitutions: Use chopped deli turkey instead of ham.
Use chopped frozen broccoli instead of peas.
Use mozzarella or Monterey Jack instead of cheddar.

steps.text: Mix and fill the egg cups.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease 6 muffin cups. Whisk 6 eggs with 2 tablespoons milk and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper.
Stir in 1/2 cup diced ham, 1/2 cup frozen peas, and 1/2 cup shredded cheddar. Divide evenly among the 6 cups.
Bake 16–18 minutes, until the centers are set. Cool 5 minutes before removing.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat briefly in the microwave or toaster oven.

title: Leftover Roasted Vegetable Quesadillas
description: A cup of leftover roasted vegetables turns into crisp cheesy quesadillas for a fast lunch instead of another reheated side dish.
substitutions: Use leftover cooked broccoli, peppers, zucchini, potatoes, or a mixture.
Add a few spoonfuls of drained beans if you want a heartier filling.

cookSteps.text: Divide 1 cup chopped leftover roasted vegetables and 1 cup shredded cheese over 2 tortillas. Top with the remaining 2 tortillas.
Heat 1 teaspoon oil or butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook each quesadilla 2–3 minutes per side, until crisp, hot, and melted.
Cut into wedges and serve with 1/4 cup salsa if using.

storage: Best served fresh. Refrigerate cooked quesadillas up to 2 days and reheat in a dry skillet.

title: Small-Batch Apple Cinnamon Rice Pudding
description: Leftover cooked rice, milk, and apple become a warm cinnamon pudding sized for a few servings.
substitutions: Use white sugar instead of brown sugar.
Use a ripe pear instead of apple.
Skip the vanilla if you do not have it.

steps.text: Simmer the rice, milk, and apple.

cookSteps.text: Combine 1 1/2 cups cooked rice, 1 1/2 cups milk, 1 diced small apple, and 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon in a medium saucepan.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat and cook 12–15 minutes, stirring often, until creamy and the apple is tender.
Stir in 3 tablespoons brown sugar and 1/2 teaspoon vanilla if using. Serve warm or chill before eating.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Stir in a splash of milk when reheating if it thickens.
